message.content:
Here are some practical, everyday tips to keep your piano sounding and looking its best: | # | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |---|-----|----------------|--------------| | 1 | **Control the humidity** | Pianos are made of wood and ivory (or synthetic). Too dry or too wet air can warp the soundboard, crack the keys, or cause the strings to stretch. | • Use a hygrometer inside the room.
• Aim for 45‑55 % RH.
• In dry climates, use a humidifier; in damp climates, use a dehumidifier.
• Keep the piano away from radiators, vents, or direct sunlight. | | 2 | **Keep it clean** | Dust, fingerprints, and grime can dull the keys and affect action. | • Wipe the keys with a soft, lint‑free cloth after each use.
• Use a piano‑specific cleaner or a mild soap solution (never spray directly on the piano).
• Avoid using harsh chemicals or abrasive pads. | | 3 | **Avoid extreme temperatures** | Rapid temperature changes can damage the wood and the internal mechanism. | • Keep the piano in a room that stays between 18–24 °C (65–75 °F).
• Don’t place it near heat sources or drafty windows. | | 4 | **Regular tuning** | Even a well‑maintained piano will drift out of tune over time. | • Tune at least twice a year (or more often if you play frequently).
• Use a professional tuner for accurate results. | | 5 | **Check the action** | Loose or sticky keys can affect playability. | • Lightly press each key; it should return smoothly.
• If a key feels sluggish, have a technician inspect the action. | | 6 | **Inspect the strings** | Broken or frayed strings can produce unwanted noises or damage the piano. | • Look for any visible cracks or frays.
• If you notice a problem, stop playing and call a technician. | | 7 | **Use a piano cover** | Protects from dust, light, and accidental knocks. | • Store a fitted cover when the piano isn’t in use. | | 8 | **Avoid heavy objects** | Dropping or leaning on the piano can damage the soundboard or frame. | • Keep the piano clear of furniture, pets, or children. | | 9 | **Professional servicing** | A full service includes cleaning, tuning, and inspection of all internal parts. | • Schedule a service every 12–18 months, or sooner if you notice any issues. | | 10 | **Keep the lid closed when not playing** | Prevents dust accumulation and protects the soundboard. | • Close the lid gently after each session. | ### Quick “Do’s & Don’ts” Checklist | Do | Don’t | |----|-------| | Keep the piano in a stable environment. | Leave it in a drafty or humid area. | | Clean the keys after each use. | Use harsh chemicals or spray cleaners directly. | | Tune regularly. | Skip tuning if you’re not hearing a problem. | | Use a cover when idle. | Leave the piano exposed to dust or light. | | Call a technician for major repairs. | Try to fix complex issues yourself. | By following these simple habits, you’ll preserve the piano’s tone, extend its life, and enjoy a reliable instrument for years to come. Happy playing!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are some tips to maintain a piano?" They want general maintenance tips. We can provide advice: humidity control, tuning, cleaning, regular checks, etc. No function call needed.
